description: I am a Computer Science student and Data Analyst passionate about space discovery, focusing on Planet X and deep-space exploration. I bring strong skills in data analysis and problem-solving to turn raw space datasets into meaningful solutions. Building this squad solo, I am looking for teammates skilled in web/app development, UI/UX design, astrophysics, and video editing/pitching. Join me to explore space data and build something impactful!
summary:
I developed a data-driven space exploration and anomaly-detection platform focused on identifying potential signatures of Planet X and uncharted deep-space objects. Using data analysis and statistical modeling, the solution processes astronomical and orbital datasets to detect subtle gravitational perturbations and irregular trajectories in the outer solar system.

This project directly addresses the challenge by transforming vast, complex space survey data into clear visualizations and prioritized candidate insights—making it faster and easier to isolate meaningful patterns from background noise.

Investigating the outer solar system is essential for advancing planetary science and understanding how our cosmic neighborhood formed and evolves. By making deep-space data analysis more intuitive, scalable, and accessible, this solution helps accelerate celestial discovery and turns raw astronomical data into actionable scientific knowledge.
details:
This project is a data-driven space exploration and orbital anomaly detection system designed to investigate potential signatures of Planet X and uncharted bodies in the outer solar system. The workflow ingests open astronomical datasets containing orbital parameters of distant celestial objects—such as Trans-Neptunian Objects (TNOs)—and cleans, normalizes, and filters the records. Using statistical modeling and anomaly-detection algorithms, it analyzes key orbital metrics including eccentricity, inclination, semi-major axis, and perihelion distance to detect unusual orbital clustering and subtle gravitational perturbations. The results are then rendered into interactive visualizations that highlight high-priority candidate anomalies against baseline solar system trajectories.

Key Benefits

  • Rapid Data Filtering: Automates the process of sifting through thousands of noisy astronomical records to isolate statistically significant orbital outliers.
  • Visual Clarity: Converts complex multi-dimensional orbital mechanics into intuitive charts and plots that are easy to interpret.
  • Accessible Exploration: Lowers the technical barrier for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts to explore deep-space survey data.

Intended Impact The primary goal of this project is to accelerate deep-space discovery by providing a scalable analytical framework for outer solar system research. By turning raw astronomical catalogs into prioritized, actionable insights, the platform supports both scientific inquiry and citizen-science exploration—helping researchers narrow down where to look next for hidden planetary bodies and advancing our understanding of how our solar system formed and evolves.

Tools, Languages, Software & Hardware Used

  • Programming Language: Python
  • Data Analysis & Modeling Libraries: Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, and Scikit-learn (for data preprocessing, statistical testing, and outlier detection)
  • Visualization & Development Environment: Matplotlib, Plotly, Jupyter Notebook, Visual Studio Code, and Git/GitHub
  • Data Sources: Publicly available orbital and small-body datasets (such as NASA/JPL Small-Body Database and Minor Planet Center catalogs)
  • Hardware: Standard personal laptop workstation

Creativity & Innovation Rather than relying solely on traditional theoretical simulations, this project applies modern data-analytics anomaly scoring directly to empirical sky-survey records. Presenting orbital perturbations as an interactive, ranked "anomaly radar" bridges the gap between raw astrophysics data and human-friendly visual storytelling.

Factors Considered Developing this project as a solo Computer Science and Data Analysis participant required careful attention to several critical factors:

  • Observational Bias & Data Noise: Accounting for incomplete sky coverage and measurement uncertainties in distant object surveys so false positives are minimized.
  • Interpretability: Ensuring every flagged anomaly is backed by transparent statistical metrics rather than a black-box score.
  • Scalability & Reproducibility: Building a lightweight, open-source pipeline that can easily ingest updated survey data as new deep-space observations are published.
